correctness.rationale: A direct stdlib polynomial-factorization and an independent SymPy finite-field factorization each exhaustively count 17,496 scalar-normalized basepoint-free binary quartic pairs, find no valid four-rational-branch case, and count exactly 576+96+192=864 three-rational-branch tame maps. Riemann–Hurwitz proves completeness after tame rational-fiber filtering; the 192 residual cases have a squarefree cubic Frobenius Wronskian factor and three distinct rational critical points. The independently scripted 576-element projective product action recovers precisely five disjoint orbits of sizes 288, 288, 72, 24 and 192. Inertia cycle arguments determine D4, V4, S4 monodromy. All three verification programs run from the embedded package directory, outputs recorded in checks.txt.

value.rationale: The maximal number of rational target branch values is a natural arithmetic ramification invariant. Even though P1(F3) has four rational points, none can all be branched by an everywhere-tame quartic cover; the sharp maximum is three. Five inequivalent attaining arithmetic types, including dihedral/Klein twists and a full symmetric-monodromy type with an additional cubic Frobenius branch orbit, completely describe the extremal stratum. This is more than a single example or arbitrary restricted count.
